key_insight: LLM-in-Sandbox shows that off-the-shelf LLMs can act like general agents by exploring a code sandbox (a virtual computer) to solve non-code tasks—without additional training. They spontaneously use the file system, external resources, and scripts to extend capability and handle complex requirements.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between LLM reasoning and actionable, environment-grounded behavior for non-code tasks—enabling models to access external knowledge, manage long contexts, and produce precise outputs without retraining or heavy prompt engineering.
method: Provide a code sandbox (virtual machine / runtime + file system) that the LLM can inspect and manipulate via generated code or shell commands.
Allow LLMs to autonomously explore: fetch external resources, read/write files to store long context, and execute scripts to format or verify outputs.
Evaluate emergent generalization by observing how standard LLMs leverage the sandbox to solve diverse, non-code tasks.
impact: Practitioners can unlock broader, agent-like capabilities from existing LLMs by giving them a simple programmable environment, reducing the need for model fine-tuning while enabling more reliable, composable workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: LLM -> Sandbox (file system + shell + runtime) -> External resources -> Final output
Before/After example: long-document handling without sandbox vs. with sandbox (file-chunking and retrieval)
Sequence flow: LLM issues command -> sandbox executes -> reads/writes files -> LLM consumes results (showing emergent tool use)
Icon set: terminal, file, web/resource, script/gear to represent core sandbox capabilities
paper_authors: Daixuan Cheng, Shaohan Huang, Yuxian Gu, Huatong Song, Guoxin Chen
